title: Advancing Neural Network Performance with Probabilistic Computing for ReLU Function
problem: Neural networks require efficient ReLU activation functions on hardware. Probabilistic computing (p-bits) offers invertible bidirectional operations but ReLU implementation details for p-circuits are underexplored.
motivation: Probabilistic computing enables bidirectional operations and invertible computation, unlocking new possibilities for neural network training and inference. Efficient p-circuit ReLU implementation improves overall probabilistic neural networks.
method: Framework for designing p-circuits using p-bits (stochastic bit representations). ReLU design using Hamiltonian method with two variants: (1) AND gate-based, (2) non-imply logic gate-based. Also designs 2x1 multiplexer and AB non-imply logic gate.
key_novelty: P-bit ReLU designs using Hamiltonian method with trade-offs between AND-based and non-imply variants; demonstrates invertible ReLU implementation and graph density optimization.
contributions: ReLU p-circuit design using Hamiltonian method
limitations: Abstract only; limited to ReLU evaluation; no full neural network demonstration; invertible property implications not explored; energy/performance metrics not provided.
primary_theme: Probabilistic computing for neural network efficiency
